extracted.intended_audience: USPTO design patent examiners; inventors, applicants, and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of USPTO training materials and resources used to instruct examiners and inform applicants/practitioners about proper prosecution, examination standards, and procedures for design patent applications (including subject-matter eligibility, obviousness, drawings, international filings, and legal analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject Matter Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training/materials listed on the page include guidance on subject matter eligibility for design patent applications; used to instruct examiners and inform applicants/practitioners about what designs qualify as patentable subject matter under applicable law and USPTO practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness analysis under 35 U.S.C. 103 (in light of LKQ v. GM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Impacts on Obviousness Analysis under 35 U.S.C. 103 for Designs in Light of LKQ Corp. V. GM Global Technology Operations LLC (Parts listed: Part 1 [FY 2024 - Q4], Part 2 [FY 2025 - Q2])
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials and training addressing how to determine obviousness of designs following the LKQ v. GM decision; informs how examiners should apply 35 U.S.C. 103 to design applications and how precedent changes obviousness analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated guidance / memorandum on making an obviousness determination (LKQ v. GM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated Guidance and Examination Instructions for Making a Determination of Obviousness in Designs in Light of LKQ Corp. v. GM Global Technology Operations LLC [22 May 2024]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memorandum providing updated examination instructions to examiners about applying the USPTO's approach to design obviousness determinations after LKQ v. GM; serves as authoritative internal policy for consistent obviousness rejections/analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of computer-generated interfaces and icons (GUI/icon guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental Guidance for Examination of Design Patent Applications Related to Computer-Generated Interfaces and Icons — Part 1: Overview of the Notice [FY 2026 - Q2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance specific to examination of GUI and icon designs, likely addressing how to treat screenshots, dynamic aspects, broken views vs. claimed views, and what constitutes the claimed ornamental design for computer-generated interfaces and icons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing Objections
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training material focused on identifying and handling drawing deficiencies in design patent applications; includes examples of drawing defects and examiner practice for issuing objections and requiring corrected drawings in accordance with drawing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of relevant Federal court decisions (Maatita, Curver, Surgisil)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Court Decisions: Maatita, Curver and Surgisil [FY 2023 - Q1]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials summarizing and explaining how specific Federal Circuit decisions affect design patent examination practice; used to teach examiners how to apply case law to examination issues (e.g., claim scope, infringement/anticipation/obviousness analysis influences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of Hague (international) design applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on processing and examining international design applications filed under the Hague Agreement, including procedural requirements, formalities, and how international filings are handled at the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to legal arguments and evaluating case law
rubrics_metrics.description: Responding to legal arguments — Part I: Understanding Case Law and the Federal Court System [Computer Based Training] [FY 2018]; Part II: How to Evaluate and Analyze Legal Arguments Based on Case Law [FY 2018]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training for examiners on how to understand, evaluate, and respond to applicants' legal arguments that rely on or reference case law; includes instruction on reading precedent, locating controlling authority, and integrating legal analysis into examination decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal analysis writing (workshop materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part II Legal Analysis Writing Workshop Slides; Part II Legal Analysis Writing Worksheet - Design Example (blank and answer key)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical exercises and slide decks intended to improve examiners' legal-writing and analytic skills for composing reasoned examination decisions, critiques, and responses that address legal issues in design prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial Design Policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy-level guidance affecting how design matters are treated within the USPTO, informing examiner practice and applicants about broader policy considerations in industrial design and design patent practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design prior-art searching using Patent Public Search (PPS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using Patent Public Search Advanced to Search Designs - YouTube
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resource demonstrating searching techniques and tools (Patent Public Search advanced) for locating prior art in design patents; supports examiner and applicant practice in conducting effective prior-art searches for design applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPEP references for design patent examination (Chapter 1500 and Chapter 2900)
rubrics_metrics.description: To find our guidance on design patent applications in the Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP), reference Chapter 1500. For additional information on international design applications, see Chapter 2900.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directive to consult the MPEP chapters that contain formal, detailed examination rules and procedures for design patents (Chapter 1500) and international design filings (Chapter 2900); these chapters constitute binding examiner guidance on many substantive and procedural points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview practice (examiner-applicant interviews)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials on conducting interviews between examiners and applicants/practitioners, covering best practices, procedural requirements, and how interviews fit into prosecution strategy and record building.
